title: Livery
description: One airline paint scheme, described part by part, precisely enough to reproduce on any airliner type. Positions are shares of each part (see docs/COORDINATES.md), so one definition fits a 737 and a 787. A livery may be described in words before it's drawn: without `fuselage` it's 'described', and a renderer falls back to the airline's standard scheme.

$schema.description: The JSON Schema this file follows, as a relative path.

id.description: Unique within the airline: lowercase words joined by hyphens, e.g. 'standard-2019', 'negus-retro'.

name.description: What spotters call it, e.g. 'Negus retro'.

kind.description: standard: the airline's fleet-wide scheme. special: one or a few airframes (promotions, state flags, anniversaries). retro: a past scheme repainted. alliance: an alliance's scheme.

from.description: When the scheme was introduced (standard) or first applied (special).

to.description: When it was retired or superseded; absent while current.

commemorates.description: For a retro: the scheme it recreates and its years, e.g. 'Negus & Negus, 1974–1980'.

description.description: The scheme in words, for people: what you'd notice first.

sources.description: Where the facts come from. Parts point back to these by index.

palette.description: The scheme's named colors; parts refer to them by name.

finish.description: The paint's finish over the whole aircraft; gloss unless said otherwise.

winglets.description: The winglets' paint: their outer and inner faces' colors, and any areas on the outer face.

areas.description: In winglet space: x 0 leading edge → 1 trailing, y 0 root → 1 tip, on the outer face.

logos.description: Each logo the scheme places: what it is (`mark`) and where it sits. The artwork itself isn't here (docs/LOGOS.md).

titles.description: Each title (lettering) the scheme carries: its words, where it sits, and the look of its type.

notes.description: Public remarks for a reader: how it was drawn and checked, and what's uncertain. No private process notes.

history.description: What the scheme replaced or was replaced by, and where its airframes went.

commonest.description: For an airline with more than one standard scheme flying (a new one being rolled out): true on the one most of its fleet wears now. A renderer that shows one scheme per airline shows this one.

drawnOn.description: The aircraft type (ICAO designator) the geometry was measured on: titles, logos and the fin's art are fixed in metres on the real aircraft, so as shares they fit that type best. Where shapes/ has that type, draw on it.

types.description: Paint that differs on one aircraft type, keyed by a shape's id in shapes/ ("B712", "A388"; an ICAO type for the types measured there): the entry's shares are measured on that shape. A renderer drawing on a shape whose id is the key, else whose types include it, lays the entry over the scheme's own paint (docs/COORDINATES.md, Paint for one type).

typePaint.description: What differs on one type. Each part given (fuselage, fin, stabilizer, wings, winglets, engines) replaces the keys it names in the scheme's part, the rest kept (areas replace the part's areas whole); titles and logos replace the scheme's lists whole; palette colors are added to the scheme's, or replace those of the same name.

note.description: What differs on this type, and from which photos.

palette.description: Colors this type's paint adds to the scheme's palette.

logos.description: This type's logos, in place of the scheme's.

titles.description: This type's titles, in place of the scheme's.

date.description: A year, a year and month, or a day.

confidence.description: high: an official source or several clear recent photos agree. medium: one good source. low: thin or conflicting evidence. approximate: drawn from memory of photos, to be checked.

title.description: What it is: a photo's caption and credit, a page's title.

note.description: What this source shows or supports, and anything to know about it.

name.description: The airline's own name for it, if published.

pantone.description: The Pantone color, where a source gives it.

ral.description: The RAL color, where a source gives it.

official.description: True when the value is published by the airline or its designers; false when matched from photos.

color.description: A palette name, or a hex value written directly.

point.description: [x, y] in the part's own space (docs/COORDINATES.md).

area.description: A region painted over the part's base, in order. A polygon (`points`), or a band between two lines across the part's length (`below`/`above`).

points.description: The area's outline, in its part's coordinates (docs/COORDINATES.md).

below.description: Paint everything under this line ([x, y] points, x ascending), only over the line's own x-range.

above.description: Paint everything over this line ([x, y] points, x ascending), only over the line's own x-range. With `below`, the band between them: `below` its upper edge, `above` its lower edge.

side.description: Which side it's painted on; both unless said otherwise.

smooth.description: true: a smooth curve through the points (a paint line that curves), sharp at the part's edges and at points marked [x, y, 1]. Default: straight lines between the points.

fuselage.description: Unrolled side: x 0 at the nose tip → 1 at the tail cone's end; y −1 the belly's centerline → 0 the side's middle → 1 the crown's centerline.

areas.description: Colored areas on the fuselage, drawn in order over its base color.

radome.description: The nose cone, where its color differs from the paint around it: its color and how far aft it reaches.

cockpitWindows.description: The windscreen's surround: 'mask' a painted band round the windows (Southwest's, many old schemes), or the base color.

windows.description: How the cabin windows show: 'plain' (dark glass), 'lined' (a dark band through them), or 'hidden' (none drawn, e.g. a wrap).

fin.description: Fin space, the left face as seen from the left: x 0 the leading edge → 1 the trailing edge (at each height), y 0 the root → 1 the tip. The rudder is x from about 0.7.

fillet.description: The dorsal fillet's paint (the curved fairing ahead of the fin's root, on types that have one), where it isn't what the fin's leading edge carries forward: easyJet's is white under an orange fin.

areas.description: Colored areas on the fin, drawn in order over its base color.

mirrored.description: True (the default) when the right face carries the design at the same fin coordinates, so it sweeps the same way relative to the direction of flight on both sides; false when the right face shows the left face's picture unreversed, so a point at (x, y) on the left face is at (1 − x, y) on the right (lettering or a flag that must read the same from both sides).

surface.description: A wing or tailplane: top and underside; areas in its space, x 0 leading edge → 1 trailing, y 0 root → 1 tip.

areas.description: Colored areas on the surface, drawn in order over its base color.

engines.description: Nacelle space: x 0 the inlet lip → 1 the exhaust; y −1 the bottom → 1 the top, on the outboard face.

inletLip.description: The polished or painted ring at the front.

areas.description: Colored areas on the nacelles, drawn in order over the cowling's color.

pylon.description: The pylon: under a wing, or the stub from the fuselage's side to a rear-mounted nacelle. Left out: under a wing as the cowling, on the fuselage as the fuselage's paint where the pylon meets it (docs/COORDINATES.md).

logo.description: A logo's place, size and colors, and what it is, described in words with a reference. Not the artwork: that's the airline's (docs/LOGOS.md).

mark.description: Which mark: an id shared across liveries, e.g. 'BAW/speedmarque', 'DAL/widget'.

licensed.description: Whose artwork it is, when it's licensed from someone other than the airline: a film studio's characters, a franchise's craft, a park's logo ("Disney", "Lucasfilm"), named as the airline's own materials credit it. It is never drawn from here; an app that leaves it out can say whose it is (docs/LOGOS.md, Licensed artwork).

at.description: The logo's center in that part's space (docs/COORDINATES.md). Points outside 0–1 are allowed and clipped to the part's outline.

height.description: Its height as a share of the part's height (fin, wings, winglets: their span, 1; fuselage, engines and belly: 2, belly to crown or bottom to top). Its width follows the artwork, which isn't here: a placeholder can be drawn square.

colors.description: The colors it's drawn in, by palette name or hex, in the artwork's order.

description.description: What it looks like, in words.

reference.description: Where to see it: the airline's brand page or a Wikimedia Commons file.

side.description: Which side it's on; both unless said otherwise.

title.description: Lettering: the airline's name or a scheme's name, its place, size and style.

at.description: The left end of the text's baseline as seen from the left side, in that part's space. On the belly: where the text starts along the fuselage, y the line its middle runs on (−1 the centerline).

height.description: Cap height, as a share of the part's height as for logos: a span of y in the part's own (unrolled) units, so the capitals' tops are at `at`'s y + height.

registration.description: The aircraft's own registration or number is lettered here (a military or government aircraft's serial: the Coast Guard's '2002'): `text` is the one on the measured aircraft, and an app that knows the aircraft's registration letters that instead, in this place, size and lettering.

parts.description: A name lettered in more than one color, as runs that spell `text` in order, each with its color (FedEx: "Fed" purple, "Ex" orange; Atlas Air: "ATLAS" navy, " AIR" gold). It's one title: one place, size and lettering, so the parts can't overlap and read in order from either side. `color` is the main one, for anything that draws a title in one color.

style.description: The lettering in words: typeface if known, weight, case, italic.

side.description: Which side it's on; both unless said otherwise.

length.description: How far the text runs (spread out to fill it), as a share of the part's x: on the fin, the chord at `at`'s height; for a rotated title, measured along the text. Without it, the text runs as its typeface sets it at that cap height.

type.description: The lettering, measured from photos: what to set it in to look right. `similar` names typefaces that come close (not a claim about what the airline used, unless `official`).

official.description: The typeface the airline or its designers name, if published.

slantDeg.description: Lean to the right, in degrees (italic or oblique).

width.description: How wide the letters are set, against the typeface's normal.

strokes.description: Even strokes (a geometric sans), thick-thin (a serif or calligraphic face), or hand-lettered.

case.description: Upper, lower or mixed case, as lettered.

xHeight.description: The lowercase letters' height (an x's) as a share of the cap height, measured off a photo: about 0.7 in most typefaces, 0.8 in easyJet's. A renderer setting the title in a stand-in typeface sizes it so the lowercase matches.

rotationDeg.description: Turned about its start, counter-clockwise as seen from the left side, as a true angle on the part as built (0 along the fuselage's axis; a fin title running up the tail is about 50–90). On the right side the placement mirrors (docs/COORDINATES.md › Right side).

mark.description: A wordmark no typeface comes close to (easyJet's, Frontier's), drawn as a mark: an id as a logo's, our own simplified shape measured from photos (docs/LOGOS.md). A renderer that has it draws it in the title's box (its baseline at `at`, its cap height `height`, stretched to `length`, its slant its own); one that doesn't sets `text` as for any title.

areaPoint.description: [x, y] in the part's own space (docs/COORDINATES.md), or [x, y, 1] for a sharp corner in a `smooth` area.
